examples.en: The CEO publicly apologized to the employees.
I admit my mistake and sincerely apologize.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 팬들에게 사죄하는 글을 올렸어요.
examples.en: The singer posted a message apologizing to the fans.

examples.ko: 약속을 어겨서 직접 만나 사죄하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I broke my promise, so I want to meet them and apologize in person.

examples.ko: 사죄할 일이 생기면 빨리 말하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If you have something to apologize for, it's better to say it quickly.

examples.ko: 회사는 피해를 본 고객들에게 사죄하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to apologize to the customers who were harmed.

explain: '사과하다'는 일상에서 가볍게도 쓰지만 '사죄하다'는 큰 잘못을 했을 때 격식 있게 써요. 친구에게 '미안해' 하는 상황에는 어울리지 않고, 뉴스나 공식 발표에서 자주 들려요. 높여 말할 때는 '사죄를 드리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '사과하다' can be used lightly in daily life, but '사죄하다' is formal and used for serious wrongdoing. It sounds out of place between friends and is common in news and official statements. The polite form is '사죄를 드리다'.

examples.en: The labor union released a statement yesterday.

examples.ko: 성명서에는 회사의 입장이 짧게 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: The statement briefly laid out the company's position.

examples.ko: 학생들이 함께 쓴 성명서가 학교 게시판에 붙었어요.
examples.en: A statement written together by the students was posted on the school bulletin board.

examples.ko: 이 성명서를 읽어 보면 상황을 이해할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you read this statement, you can understand the situation.

examples.ko: 시민 단체는 성명서로 정부에 의견을 전했어요.
examples.en: The civic group conveyed its opinion to the government through a statement.
Even a short statement has to be written accurately.

explain: 단체나 회사가 공식 입장을 글로 낼 때 써요. 말로 하는 발표는 '발표'나 '성명'이라고 하고, 글로 낼 때 '성명서'라고 해요. 보통 '성명서를 내다', '성명서를 발표하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when a group or company puts its official position in writing. A spoken announcement is '발표' or '성명'; the written document is '성명서'. It usually appears as '성명서를 내다' or '성명서를 발표하다'.

examples.en: I have a friend who works at a new company.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 신생 카페가 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Many new cafes have opened in this neighborhood.
I can hear a baby crying in the newborn nursery.
The newly founded countries decided to join forces.

examples.ko: 올해 신생 팀이 처음으로 경기에 나갔어요.
examples.en: This year the new team played its first match.

examples.ko: 신생 업체는 처음 몇 년이 가장 힘들어요.
examples.en: A new business has the hardest time in its first few years.

explain: '신생'은 혼자 쓰기보다 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요. 갓 태어난 아기는 '신생아', 새로 생긴 회사나 나라는 '신생 기업', '신생국'이에요. 오래된 것은 '기존', 새로 나온 것은 '신생'으로 대비해 말해요.
explain_en: '신생' is rarely used alone; it attaches to another word. A newborn baby is '신생아', and a newly founded company or country is '신생 기업' or '신생국'. It contrasts with '기존' (existing).

en: have a premonition; have a hunch

examples.ko: 아침부터 좋은 일이 생길 것 같다고 예감했어요.
examples.en: Since morning I had a feeling something good would happen.

examples.ko: 그는 시험에 떨어질 것을 예감하고 있었어요.
examples.en: He sensed that he would fail the exam.
When the phone rang, I sensed bad news.
I have a hunch that our team will win.

examples.ko: 어머니는 제가 올 줄 미리 예감하셨대요.
examples.en: My mother says she sensed ahead of time that I would come.

examples.ko: 비가 올 것을 예감하는 사람처럼 우산을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed an umbrella like someone who senses rain coming.

explain: '예감하다'는 이유 없이 마음으로 미리 느낄 때 써요. 근거를 들어 미리 맞히는 '예상하다', '예측하다'와 달라요. 그래서 '예감이 좋다/나쁘다'처럼 명사로도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '예감하다' is for sensing something in advance with no clear reason. It differs from '예상하다' and '예측하다', which rely on evidence. People often use the noun form too, as in '예감이 좋다/나쁘다'.

examples.en: Today is a lucky day.

examples.ko: 길에서 돈을 주운 걸 보니 오늘은 운수가 좋은가 봐요.
examples.en: Finding money on the street, today must be my lucky day.

examples.ko: 운수 나쁜 날에는 모든 일이 꼬여요.
examples.en: On an unlucky day everything goes wrong.

examples.ko: 할머니는 새해마다 한 해 운수를 보러 가세요.
examples.en: Every New Year my grandmother goes to have her fortune for the year read.
Winning the lottery, what great luck!
I'll leave it to luck and just try.

explain: '운수'는 그날그날 일이 잘 풀리는 정도를 말할 때 써요. '운'보다 조금 옛스럽고, '운수 좋은 날'처럼 굳은 말로 많이 나와요. 한 해 전체의 운을 점칠 때는 '운세'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: '운수' describes how well things tend to go on a given day. It sounds slightly more old-fashioned than '운' and appears in set phrases like '운수 좋은 날'. For the luck of a whole year, '운세' is used more often.

examples.en: There are many tall buildings in central Seoul.

examples.ko: 도시 중심부까지 지하철로 십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes ten minutes by subway to reach the city center.
The wind is much stronger at the center of the typhoon.
The square is in the center of the village.

examples.ko: 이 사건의 중심부에는 한 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was one person at the heart of this case.
The closer you get to the center, the more expensive the housing becomes.

explain: '중심'은 한가운데 점이나 중요한 점을, '중심부'는 한가운데 넓은 부분을 가리켜요. '도시 중심부'처럼 면적이 있는 곳에 써요. 가운데 거리를 말하는 '시내', '도심'과 비슷하지만 '중심부'는 도시가 아닌 것에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '중심' is the middle point or what matters most, while '중심부' is a broad central region, as in '도시 중심부'. It resembles '시내' and '도심', but '중심부' also works for things that are not cities, like a typhoon.

examples.en: The government collects taxes based on income.
The city hall is collecting parking fees.
The club collected dues every month.
The tax office is in charge of collecting taxes.

examples.ko: 벌금을 징수할 때는 영수증을 줘야 해요.
examples.en: When collecting a fine, you must give a receipt.

examples.ko: 새 제도가 생겨서 요금을 따로 징수하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Under the new system, they decided to charge the fee separately.

explain: '징수하다'는 국가나 단체가 세금, 요금을 걷을 때 써요. 돈을 내는 사람은 '납부하다'라고 해서 짝이 돼요. 친구들끼리 돈을 모을 때는 '걷다', '모으다'라고 말하고 '징수하다'는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: '징수하다' is used when a state or organization collects taxes or fees. The person who pays uses '납부하다', so the two pair up. Friends gathering money say '걷다' or '모으다', never '징수하다'.

examples.ko: 여름에는 모기 퇴치 스프레이가 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: In summer you really need a mosquito repellent spray.

examples.ko: 정부가 질병 퇴치를 위해 예산을 늘렸어요.
examples.en: The government increased its budget to eradicate the disease.
We left the cockroach extermination to a professional company.

examples.ko: 쥐 퇴치에 효과가 좋은 방법이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a method that works well for getting rid of mice.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 잡초 퇴치 작업을 함께 했어요.
examples.en: The villagers worked together on clearing out the weeds.
Eradicating the infectious disease is the biggest goal.

explain: '퇴치'는 모기, 쥐, 병처럼 해로운 것을 없앨 때 써요. 약이나 방법을 말할 때 '모기 퇴치제', '해충 퇴치'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여 써요.
explain_en: 퇴치 is used for getting rid of harmful things like mosquitoes, rats or diseases. For a product or method, put the target first: '모기 퇴치제', '해충 퇴치'.

examples.ko: 약을 뿌려서 집 안의 벌레를 퇴치했어요.
examples.en: I sprayed insecticide and got rid of the bugs in the house.
To eradicate this disease, a vaccine is needed.
Farmers research ways to get rid of pests.

examples.ko: 모기를 퇴치할 수 있는 식물이 있대요.
examples.en: They say there are plants that can repel mosquitoes.
The village became quiet after getting rid of the rats.
It took a long time to completely wipe out the epidemic.

explain: '없애다'는 뭐든 쓸 수 있지만 '퇴치하다'는 벌레, 병, 해로운 풀처럼 해로운 대상에 써요. '짐을 퇴치하다'처럼 말하면 어색해요. 어려운 대상일수록 '완전히 퇴치하다'처럼 자주 같이 써요.
explain_en: '없애다' can be used for anything, but 퇴치하다 is for harmful targets such as insects, diseases and harmful weeds. Saying '짐을 퇴치하다' (get rid of luggage) sounds odd. For hard targets it often appears as '완전히 퇴치하다'.

examples.en: The company dismissed the director whose wrongdoing came to light.
The club decided to dismiss the manager.
The board can remove the president.

examples.ko: 성적이 나빠서 감독을 해임하라는 목소리가 커졌어요.
examples.en: Calls to dismiss the coach grew louder because of poor results.
They dismissed him and hired a new person.

examples.ko: 학교는 교장을 해임해 달라는 요청을 받았어요.
examples.en: The school received a request to remove the principal.

explain: '해임하다'는 직책이나 자리를 맡은 사람을 그 자리에서 물러나게 할 때 써요. 일반 직원을 내보내는 '해고하다'와 달리 회사 전체가 아니라 맡은 직책에서만 물러나게 할 수도 있어요. 스스로 그만두면 '사임하다'를 써요.
explain_en: '해임하다' means removing someone from a post. Unlike '해고하다' (fire from the job), it can mean removal from a position only. If the person leaves by choice, use '사임하다'.

examples.en: The farmers got together and formed a cooperative.

examples.ko: 우리 동네에는 주민이 운영하는 협동조합 가게가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a cooperative store run by residents in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 협동조합에 가입하면 싸게 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you join the cooperative, you can buy things cheaply.
A cooperative shares its profits among its members.
University students opened a cooperative cafe.

examples.ko: 그 우유는 낙농 협동조합에서 만든 거예요.
examples.en: That milk was made by a dairy cooperative.

explain: '협동조합'은 일반 회사와 달리 낸 돈의 크기가 아니라 사람 한 명이 한 표를 가져요. 농업 쪽은 '농협', 생활용품 쪽은 '생협'처럼 줄여서 부르는 일이 많아요. 가입한 사람은 '조합원'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike an ordinary company, a cooperative gives each person one vote regardless of how much they put in. Shortened names are common, such as '농협' for farming and '생협' for consumer goods. A member is called a '조합원'.

en: live in harmony; unite; get along

examples.en: Our class gets along and helps each other.

examples.ko: 다른 나라 사람들과 화합하는 법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned how to live in harmony with people from other countries.
The sports day is a good chance for students to come together.

examples.ko: 두 가족이 화합하고 나서 분위기가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: The mood improved after the two families came together.
Work goes well only when the staff are in harmony.

examples.ko: 회식은 팀이 화합할 수 있게 도와줘요.
examples.en: Company dinners help the team to bond.

explain: '화합하다'는 사람이나 집단이 다툼 없이 마음을 모을 때 써요. '단결하다'는 같은 목표로 뭉치는 느낌이 강하고, '화합하다'는 사이좋게 어울리는 느낌이 커요. 물건에는 쓰지 않고 사람에게만 써요.
explain_en: '화합하다' is for people or groups joining hearts without conflict. '단결하다' stresses banding together for a goal, while '화합하다' stresses getting along. It is used for people, never things.

examples.en: I had coffee during the break.
Let's stop for a short rest at the highway rest area.
A new sofa has been put in the staff lounge.

examples.ko: 공원에 휴게 공간이 있어서 앉아서 쉴 수 있어요.
examples.en: The park has a rest area where you can sit down.
The lunch break is one hour.

examples.ko: 운전할 때는 두 시간마다 휴게소에 들르세요.
examples.en: When driving, stop at a rest area every two hours.

explain: '휴게'는 혼자 쓰이는 일이 거의 없고 '휴게소', '휴게실', '휴게 시간'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙어요. '휴식'은 쉬는 일 자체를, '휴게'는 쉬는 곳이나 시간을 나타낼 때 더 자주 나와요. 고속도로에서 보이는 '휴게소'가 가장 흔한 예예요.
explain_en: '휴게' almost never stands alone; it attaches to words like '휴게소', '휴게실' or '휴게 시간'. '휴식' names the act of resting, while '휴게' more often marks a place or time for it. The '휴게소' on highways is the most common example.

examples.en: Turn right at the next intersection.
At an intersection you have to watch the signals carefully.
There is a convenience store in front of the big intersection.
The cars almost collided at the intersection.
That intersection is always jammed.
My house is right after the intersection.

explain: 길이 만나는 곳을 '사거리', '삼거리'처럼 갈래 수로 부르는 일이 많아요. '교차로'는 이런 곳을 통틀어 부르는 공식적인 말이에요. 길을 알려 줄 때는 '사거리에서 우회전하세요'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Koreans usually name junctions by the number of roads, like '사거리' or '삼거리'. '교차로' is the formal umbrella term. When giving directions, '사거리에서 우회전하세요' sounds more natural.

examples.en: At the ski resort I rode the lift up to the top.
The lift suddenly stopped and I was a little scared.

examples.ko: 리프트 표는 매표소에서 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy lift tickets at the ticket office.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 리프트 운행이 중단됐어요.
examples.en: The lift stopped running because of the heavy snow.
In winter the line in front of the lift is long.
The view looking down from the lift was really beautiful.

explain: 한국에서 '리프트'는 주로 스키장이나 관광지의 의자 리프트를 가리켜요. 건물 안에서 타는 것은 '엘리베이터'라고 하고 '리프트'라고 하지 않아요. 휠체어용 승강 장치도 '휠체어 리프트'라고 불러요.
explain_en: In Korea, '리프트' mostly means a chair lift at ski resorts or tourist sites. The thing you ride inside buildings is an '엘리베이터', not a '리프트'. A wheelchair platform lift is '휠체어 리프트'.

examples.en: This cafe has a really nice atmosphere.
The mood of the room changed once I swapped the lighting.

examples.ko: 오늘은 조용한 무드의 음악이 듣고 싶어요.
examples.en: Today I want to listen to music with a quiet, calm feel.

examples.ko: 영화 속 무드가 너무 어두워서 보기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The mood in the movie was so dark that it was hard to watch.
I lit candles to create a romantic mood.

examples.ko: 무드 있는 가게라서 데이트 장소로 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: It's a stylish place, so it's popular for dates.

explain: '무드'는 영어 mood에서 온 말이지만 한국어에서는 주로 장소, 음악, 사진의 분위기를 말해요. 사람 기분은 '기분'이라고 하고 '무드'라고 하지 않아요. '무드 있다', '무드를 잡다'처럼 로맨틱한 분위기 얘기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '무드' comes from English 'mood', but in Korean it mostly describes the atmosphere of a place, music or a photo. A person's feelings are '기분', not '무드'. It often appears in romantic contexts like '무드 있다' or '무드를 잡다'.

examples.en: The team leader divided the work evenly among the team members.

examples.ko: 시간을 잘 배분하면 시험을 다 풀 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you allocate your time well, you can finish the whole test.
Please divide the leftover snacks equally among the kids.
Allocating the budget is the hardest part.
You need a standard when distributing profits.
The company decided to distribute the bonus among its employees.

explain: '배분하다'는 정해진 양의 돈, 시간, 일을 여러 곳에 나눠 줄 때 써요. 물건을 손에 쥐여 주는 '나눠 주다'와 달리 몫을 정하는 느낌이 있어요. '분배하다'와 거의 같지만 '배분하다'는 일과 시간에도 자연스럽게 써요.
explain_en: '배분하다' is for splitting a set amount of money, time or work across several places or people. Unlike '나눠 주다' (hand out), it carries the sense of deciding shares. It is nearly the same as '분배하다', but '배분하다' feels more natural with work and time.

examples.en: Fans were surprised by the news of the manager's resignation.
The president announced his resignation for health reasons.

examples.ko: 그의 사임 이유는 아직 알려지지 않았어요.
examples.en: The reason for his resignation hasn't been made public yet.
The minister expressed his intention to resign.

examples.ko: 사임 이후에도 그는 회사를 돕고 있어요.
examples.en: Even after stepping down, he still helps the company.
The company is in turmoil because of the CEO's sudden resignation.

explain: '사임'은 맡은 직책을 스스로 내려놓는 일이에요. 같은 직책 이야기에서 회사가 내보내면 '해임', 평직원이 그만두면 '퇴사'를 써요. 높은 자리에서 물러난다는 느낌이라 일반 아르바이트에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: '사임' is stepping down from a post by one's own choice. If the company removes the person it's '해임', and when an ordinary employee quits it's '퇴사'. It suggests leaving a high position, so it doesn't fit a part-time job.

examples.en: The manager stepped down because of poor results.
The CEO plans to resign next month.
He decided to resign and take responsibility.
On the day he resigned, he left a letter for the staff.
The university president resigned suddenly, and the school became noisy with talk.
After resigning, he went back to his hometown.

explain: '사임하다'는 높은 직책에서 스스로 물러날 때 써요. 일반 회사를 그만두는 말은 '퇴사하다'이고, '그만두다'가 가장 일상적이에요. 윗사람이 내보내는 경우는 '해임하다'라서 누가 결정했는지가 달라요.
explain_en: '사임하다' is for stepping down from a high post by choice. Leaving an ordinary company is '퇴사하다', and '그만두다' is the everyday word. If a superior removes the person it's '해임하다', so who decides differs.

examples.en: I check my daily horoscope every morning.

examples.ko: 새해에는 한 해 운세를 보러 가는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people go to have their fortune for the year read at New Year.
I heard that my fortune is good this year.
My friend checked my fortune using an app.

examples.ko: 운세에 너무 매달리지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to rely too much on fortune telling.

examples.ko: 신문 맨 뒤에는 띠별 운세가 실려 있어요.
examples.en: The zodiac fortunes are printed on the back page of the newspaper.

explain: '운세'는 한 해, 한 달, 하루의 운이 어떻게 흘러갈지를 점쳐서 보는 것을 말할 때 써요. 그날그날 일이 풀리는 정도를 말하는 '운수'와 달리 '운세를 보다/풀이하다'로 점과 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 띠나 별자리별 운세를 자주 봐요.
explain_en: 운세 is used for reading how your luck will go over a year, a month or a day. Unlike 운수, the luck of the moment, it is often used together with fortune-telling, as in '운세를 보다/풀이하다'. People often check the 운세 for their zodiac animal or star sign.

examples.en: That drama is re-aired on weekend mornings.
The broadcaster rebroadcast the popular program.

examples.ko: 어제 못 본 경기를 밤에 재방송한대요.
examples.en: They say they'll re-air the game I missed yesterday tonight.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 재방송하는 시간이 매번 달라요.
examples.en: The re-air time for this program is different each time.

examples.ko: 재방송할 때는 자막을 넣어 달라고 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I asked them to add subtitles when they re-air it.

examples.ko: 뉴스는 저녁에 한 번 더 재방송하고 있어요.
examples.en: The news is being rebroadcast once more in the evening.

explain: '재방송하다'는 이미 방송한 것을 한 번 더 내보낼 때 써요. 시청자는 '재방송으로 보다'라고 하고, 처음 나가는 방송은 '본방'이라고 불러요. '본방 사수'는 재방송 말고 실시간으로 꼭 본다는 뜻의 인기 있는 표현이에요.
explain_en: '재방송하다' is used when a program that already aired is shown once more. Viewers say '재방송으로 보다', and the first airing is called '본방'. '본방 사수' is a popular phrase for making sure to watch the live broadcast.

en: founding; establishment (of a team or group)

examples.ko: 이 야구팀은 올해로 창단 삼십 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: This baseball team is thirty years old this year.
Many fans gathered at the founding anniversary ceremony.

examples.ko: 우리 합창 모임은 창단 이후 처음으로 해외 공연을 해요.
examples.en: The choir is performing abroad for the first time since it was founded.
The founding members still gather in the practice room.
The founding of an orchestra at our school has been decided.

examples.ko: 창단 첫해에 우승을 해서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: They won the championship in their first year and became a hot topic.

explain: '창단'은 야구팀, 합창단, 무용단처럼 '단'이 붙는 단체를 처음 만들 때 써요. 일반 모임이나 회사에는 '설립', '창립'이라고 해요. 운동 구단은 '구단 창단', 연주 단체는 '창단 공연'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: '창단' is for founding a group whose name ends in '단', such as a baseball team, choir or dance company. For ordinary clubs or companies, '설립' or '창립' is used. You often hear '구단 창단' or '창단 공연'.

examples.ko: 이 길은 차가 통행할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Cars cannot pass along this road.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 산길을 통행하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to get through the mountain road because of heavy snow.

examples.ko: 밤 열 시 이후에는 이 다리를 통행하지 못해요.
examples.en: You cannot cross this bridge after ten at night.
Because of construction, people can only pass on one side.

examples.ko: 좁은 골목을 통행하는 차들은 천천히 달려요.
examples.en: Cars passing through the narrow alley drive slowly.
To pass safely, watch the signs carefully.

explain: '통행하다'는 길이나 다리, 문을 지나다닐 때 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서는 '다니다', '지나가다'라고 말하고, '통행하다'는 표지판이나 공지에서 더 자주 보여요. '통행금지', '일방통행'은 실제 길에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: '통행하다' is a stiff word for passing along a road, bridge or gate. In daily speech people say '다니다' or '지나가다', and '통행하다' appears more on signs and notices. '통행금지' and '일방통행' are common sights on real roads.

examples.en: Sunflowers have bloomed fully in the field.
Sunflowers bloom with yellow flowers in summer.
My grandmother shelled sunflower seeds for me.

examples.ko: 여름 여행 때 해바라기 밭에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: On my summer trip I took pictures in a sunflower field.
I hung a sunflower painting by the window.
I looked up at the tall sunflower.

explain: 해를 따라 움직이는 모습에서 생긴 이름이에요. 노란 꽃잎이 크고 둥글어서 여름 꽃의 대표로 꼽혀요. 꽃이 지고 나면 먹는 씨앗이 남는데, 이것을 '해바라기씨'라고 해요.
explain_en: The name comes from how the flower seems to follow the sun. Its big, round yellow petals make it a symbol of summer flowers. After it fades, the edible seeds are called '해바라기씨'.

examples.ko: 이 청소기는 흡입 힘이 아주 좋아요.
examples.en: This vacuum cleaner has very strong suction.
If you inhale smoke, you cough.

examples.ko: 흡입 구멍이 막혀서 물이 안 빠져요.
examples.en: The suction hole is blocked, so the water doesn't drain.
That medicine is taken by breathing it in through the mouth.
I wore a mask to avoid breathing in dust.
I cleaned the air intake of the air conditioner.

explain: 기계가 공기나 물을 빨아들일 때, 몸이 가스나 먼지를 들이마실 때 모두 써요. 일상에서는 '빨아들이다', '들이마시다'가 더 흔하고, '흡입'은 설명서나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요. '흡입력', '흡입구'로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It covers both machines pulling in air or water and bodies breathing in gas or dust. In everyday speech '빨아들이다' or '들이마시다' are more common, while '흡입' shows up in manuals and news. It also forms '흡입력' and '흡입구'.

examples.en: In the article the victim's name appeared as a pseudonym.
It's fine to use an alias during the interview.
This name is not my real name but an alias.
The reporter used an alias to protect the source.

examples.ko: 가명 뒤에 숨은 사람이 누군지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I'm curious who is hiding behind the alias.
We used aliases in the survey results.

explain: '가명'은 본명을 숨기려고 쓰는 이름이고, 작가나 가수가 일부러 정한 이름은 '필명', '예명'이라고 해요. 글에서 학생 이름을 감출 때처럼 개인 정보를 지키는 용도로도 자주 써요. 반대말은 '본명'이에요.
explain_en: '가명' is a name used to hide the real one. A writer's chosen name is '필명' and an entertainer's is '예명'. It is often used to protect personal information, and its opposite is '본명'.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 환자의 폐를 꼼꼼하게 검진했어요.
examples.en: The doctor examined the patient's lungs carefully.
I went to the pediatrician to have the baby examined.

examples.ko: 오늘 검진한 결과는 다음 주에 나와요.
examples.en: The results of today's checkup will come out next week.

examples.ko: 치아를 검진하고 나서 치료 계획을 세웠어요.
examples.en: After the dental checkup, we made a treatment plan.
The company gives employees free checkups.

examples.ko: 검진하러 갈 때는 아침을 먹지 말고 가세요.
examples.en: When you go for a checkup, don't eat breakfast.

explain: '검진하다'는 아픈 곳이 없어도 건강한지 정기적으로 살펴볼 때 써요. 아픈 곳이 있어서 의사를 만나는 '진찰받다', '진료받다'와 달라요. 보통 '건강검진을 받다'라고 말하고, '검진하다'는 의사나 병원이 주어일 때 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '검진하다' is for routine checks on whether you are healthy, even with no symptoms. It differs from '진찰받다' or '진료받다', which means seeing a doctor for a problem. Patients usually say '건강검진을 받다', and '검진하다' fits better when the doctor or hospital is the subject.

examples.en: Ramen has a lot of sodium in it.
I left the broth to cut down on sodium.

examples.ko: 한국 사람들은 나트륨을 많이 먹는 편이에요.
examples.en: Koreans tend to eat a lot of sodium.
This snack has a low sodium content.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 나트륨이 적은 음식을 먹으라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to eat food low in sodium.
Check the sodium amount on the packaging.

explain: 영양 성분표에서 '나트륨'은 소금에 들어 있는 성분이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '짜게 먹다', '염분'이라고 더 자주 말해요. 건강 뉴스에서는 '나트륨 줄이기'처럼 자주 보여요.
explain_en: On nutrition labels '나트륨' is the component found in salt. In daily talk people more often say '짜게 먹다' or '염분'. In health news it appears in phrases like '나트륨 줄이기'.

examples.en: The child scribbled on the wall with crayons.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 공책에 낙서하다가 선생님께 들켰어요.
examples.en: I was scribbling in my notebook during class and the teacher noticed.
You must not doodle on the desk.

examples.ko: 심심할 때 종이에 낙서하는 걸 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like doodling on paper when I'm bored.
Someone has scribbled on the bathroom door.
I was doodling on a memo pad while on the phone.

explain: '낙서하다'는 마음대로 쓰거나 그리는 일이에요. 공책이나 종이에 하면 괜찮지만 벽이나 책상 같은 공공장소에 하면 잘못으로 여겨요. 의미 있는 그림을 그리는 '그리다'와 달리 장난스럽고 가벼운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '낙서하다' is writing or drawing freely without much purpose. On a notebook or paper it is harmless, but on walls or desks in public places it counts as misbehavior. Unlike '그리다', it feels playful and casual.

examples.en: I jumped from the plane wearing a parachute.
Once the parachute opened, I began to come down slowly.
I attached a parachute to the box and dropped it.
The rescue team sent supplies down by parachute.
Parachute training is very dangerous.
The kids played a parachute game on the playground.

explain: 비행기에서 뛰어내릴 때 쓰는 도구예요. 한국어에서는 여기서 나온 '낙하산 인사'라는 말이 더 자주 들려요. 실력이 아니라 연줄로 높은 자리에 오른 사람을 부정적으로 말할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 새 사장이 낙하산 인사라서 직원들이 불만이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실력이 아닌 연줄로 높은 자리에 간 사람을 비판할 때 써요. 대부분 부정적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically for someone placed in a high position through connections rather than merit. It is almost always negative.

explain_en: It is the equipment used when jumping from an airplane. In Korean, the derived phrase '낙하산 인사' is heard even more often, a negative term for someone placed in a high post through connections rather than ability.

examples.ko: 세금을 이번 달 말까지 납부해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay the tax by the end of this month.
You can pay the tuition at the bank.
If you don't pay the maintenance fee, a late fee is added.
I pay the insurance premium automatically every month.
After paying the fine, I received a receipt.
I paid the bill easily with the app.

explain: '납부하다'는 세금, 요금, 등록금처럼 정해진 곳에 정해진 돈을 낼 때 써요. 가게에서 물건값을 내는 '계산하다', '내다'와 달라요. 받는 쪽은 '징수하다'를 쓰니까 서로 짝이에요.
explain_en: '납부하다' is for paying a fixed amount to a designated place, such as taxes, bills or tuition. It differs from '계산하다' or '내다', used when paying in a shop. The receiving side uses '징수하다', so the two pair up.

examples.en: There is a wide swamp behind the village.
If you fall into a swamp, it's hard to get out by yourself.
Rare birds live in this swamp.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 길이 늪처럼 변했어요.
examples.en: With so much rain, the road turned into a bog.
There are so many mosquitoes near the swamp.
People gathered to protect the wetland.

explain: '늪'은 땅이 질고 물이 고여서 깊이 빠지는 곳이에요. '습지'는 물기가 많은 땅 전체를 부르는 더 넓은 말이에요. '게임의 늪', '빚의 늪'처럼 빠져나오기 어려운 상황을 비유해서도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 게임의 늪에 빠져서 공부를 못 했어요.
phrases.en: get stuck in a hole you can't climb out of
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 습관이나 상황에 깊이 빠져서 나오기 어려울 때 써요. '빚의 늪', '게임의 늪'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone sinks into a bad habit or situation and cannot get out, as in '빚의 늪' or '게임의 늪'.

explain_en: A '늪' is wet, muddy ground where you sink deeply. '습지' is the wider term for any waterlogged land. It is also used metaphorically for situations that are hard to escape, as in '빚의 늪'.

examples.ko: 그 고양이는 도도해서 잘 안 안겨요.
examples.en: That cat is aloof and doesn't let itself be held easily.
The way she walked by with a haughty expression was striking.

examples.ko: 처음에는 도도해 보였지만 알고 보니 수줍음이 많았어요.
examples.en: At first she looked aloof, but it turned out she was just shy.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 도도하게 인사만 하고 떠났어요.
examples.en: The actress only gave a haughty greeting and left.
If you are too aloof, it's hard to make friends.

examples.ko: 도도한 성격이라서 쉽게 마음을 열지 않아요.
examples.en: She has an aloof personality and doesn't open up easily.

explain: '도도하다'는 잘난 척한다기보다 쉽게 다가가기 어려운 자신감 있는 태도에 써요. '거만하다'는 잘난 척하며 남을 낮춰 보는 부정적인 말이에요. '도도하다'는 그보다 도시적이고 멋있게 느껴지는 경우도 있어요.
explain_en: '도도하다' describes a confident manner that's hard to approach, less showing off than keeping distance. '거만하다' is clearly negative, looking down on others. '도도하다' can sometimes feel cool and stylish.

examples.ko: 호수 위에 하얀 백조가 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A white swan is floating on the lake.
Swans move to warmer places in winter.
The kids tried to give bread to the swan.
I played the role of the swan in the ballet performance.

examples.ko: 백조 한 쌍이 물가를 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: A pair of swans walked slowly along the water's edge.
I saw a swan for the first time at the park pond.

explain: '백조'는 한자로 '흰 새'라는 뜻을 가진 말이지만 보통 큰 물새를 가리켜요. 순우리말로는 '고니'라고 해요. 발레 '백조의 호수'로도 잘 알려져 있어요.
explain_en: The Hanja means 'white bird', but the word refers to a large water bird. The native Korean word is 고니. It is also well known from the ballet 'Swan Lake' (백조의 호수).

examples.en: The classroom suddenly became rowdy.

examples.ko: 밖이 너무 소란해서 잠을 잘 수 없어요.
examples.en: It's so noisy outside that I can't sleep.
The meeting began in a commotion.
The market is always noisy but full of life.
It's noisy over there, so let's go look.
I quieted the kids who were making a racket.

explain: '시끄럽다'는 소리가 크다는 느낌이고, '소란하다'는 여러 사람이 떠들거나 일이 터져서 어수선한 분위기에 써요. 소리뿐 아니라 어지러운 상황을 말해서 '소란한 분위기'처럼 써요. '소란을 피우다'처럼 명사로도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: '시끄럽다' stresses loud sound, while '소란하다' suits a chaotic atmosphere when many people are making noise or something has erupted. It covers disorder, not only sound. The noun appears in '소란을 피우다' (make a scene).

examples.en: My grandfather is still active and energetic.
Kids have a hearty appetite, so they eat a lot.
When spring comes, the trees grow vigorously.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 왕성한 창작 활동으로 유명해요.
examples.en: That writer is famous for his prolific creative work.

examples.ko: 호기심이 왕성한 학생이 질문을 많이 해요.
examples.en: A student with great curiosity asks many questions.
You have to be healthy for your stamina to be strong.

explain: '왕성하다'는 식욕, 호기심, 활동처럼 힘이 넘쳐서 활발할 때 써요. '건강하다'는 몸 상태 전체를 말하고, '왕성하다'는 그 힘이 눈에 띄게 드러난다는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '식욕이 왕성하다', '왕성한 활동'처럼 짝이 정해져 있어요.
explain_en: '왕성하다' is used when appetite, curiosity or activity is overflowing with energy. '건강하다' describes overall condition, while '왕성하다' implies the vitality is clearly visible. It usually pairs with fixed words, as in '식욕이 왕성하다' or '왕성한 활동'.
